intro: Lesson 60: Metals and non-metals. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Safety guide: the home property test
points: Use only clean dry objects: spoon, foil, pencil, eraser
Magnet test only; no batteries or mains
Never put magnets near phones or cards

keywords.def: lets heat or electricity pass through easily

questions.q: Why are electrical plugs covered in plastic?
questions.a: Plastic is an insulator, so it stops electric shocks

questions.q: Core: Test six household objects (steel spoon, foil, pencil lead, plastic ruler, coin, eraser) for shiny, magnetic and sonorous. Decide metal or non-metal.
questions.a: Table of observations; spoon, foil, coin metals; ruler, eraser non-metals; pencil lead (graphite) a non-metal that looks shiny

questions.q: Extend: Explain why aluminium is used for drinks cans and aeroplane bodies.
questions.a: Light, malleable, does not rust easily

questions.q: Stretch: Graphite conducts electricity. Why is it still classed as a non-metal?
questions.a: Its other properties are non-metal ones: it is brittle, not malleable or ductile, and carbon sits on the non-metal side of the periodic table

questions.q: Copper is used for wires because it is...
options: Ductile and a good electrical conductor
questions.a: B) Ductile and a good electrical conductor. Wires need a metal that can be drawn out and conducts well.

questions.q: Big question: why are pan handles plastic or wood?
questions.a: They are insulators, so they stay cool.
